newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Hypo raises capital to PLN 89.5 mln.
newsitem.headline: Polish Hypo raises capital to PLN 89.5 mln.

text.p: Hypo-Bank Polska SA, a fully owned subsidiary of Germany's Bayerische Hypotheken und Wechsel Bank AG, in October raised its capital to 89.5 million zlotys from 34 million zlotys, the bank's president said on Wednesday.
Jrg Dorka told a news conference the capital rise showed the bank's conviction that Poland's growing economy made the country an attractive place to do business.
"The capital rise shows our conviction that Poland, as one of the fastest growing European countries, is a place with a future," Dorka said.

He said Hypo-Bank, which now has one branch in the western town of Poznan, was already building another branch in the town of Wroclaw and next year planned to open branches in Katowice, Krakow, Szczecin and Gdansk.
Hypo's deputy president Wlodzimierz Kicinski, also present, said half of the bank's institutional clients were foreign companies and that foreign individual clients slightly outnumbered Polish ones.

He also said Hypo, which had a balance sheet total of 130.7 million zlotys on October 31, was testing an electronic banking system for its clients enabling them to do business with the bank whenever then wanted via a direct computer link.
"Electronic banking has been made possible by Hypo-Bank's joining the modern electronic interbank clearing system Elixir," Kicinski said.
Kicinski said the bank, which started full operations in Poland in January this year and employs 61, did not expect any profit in 1996.
